prompt: What is new in C++20 and C++23?
completion:
Below is a high‑level “what‑is‑new” summary that compares the two most recent C++ standards that are already published (C++20) and the first one that is being finalized (C++23). The focus is on language changes (syntax, semantics, compiler‑level rules) and the Standard Library additions that shipped with each revision. If you need a deeper dive into any item, let me know and I can provide the relevant proposal numbers and a short technical note. --- ## 1. C++20 – 2020 ### Language (syntax & semantics) | Feature | What it adds | |---------|--------------| | **Modules** (`export module`, `import`) | First real module system in C++ – eliminates pre‑processor include headaches. | | **Concepts** (`concept`, `requires`, `typename T = U`, …) | Compile‑time constraints on template parameters, improving diagnostics and expressiveness. | | **Ranges** (`std::ranges`, `views`, `actions`) | A modern, composable view of containers/iterators, replacing many uses of ``/iterator loops. | | **Coroutines** (`co_await`, `co_yield`, `co_return`) | Lightweight async generators/iterators; used by `std::generator`‑style types. | | **`constexpr` Enhancements** | Full `constexpr` support for most of the standard library; `consteval` and `constinit`; `constexpr` constructors for user‑defined types; `constexpr` if‑constexpr; `constexpr` lambdas; `constexpr` `std::bitset` operations. | | **`char8_t` & UTF‑8 literals** | New 8‑bit character type and `u8""` string literal type. | | **`std::span`** | Fixed‑size, non‑owning view of contiguous memory (C++11‑style but with bounds safety). | | **`std::format`** | Standard, locale‑aware, type‑safe formatting (similar to Python’s f‑strings or `fmt`). | | **`std::chrono` Calendar/Timezone** | `year_month_day`, `sys_days`, `utc_clock`, `time_zone`, `zoned_time`, `offset_time`. | | **`std::filesystem`** | Cross‑platform file system API (paths, iterators, attributes). | | **`std::bit_cast`** | Compile‑time reinterpretation of bit representation (no UB). | | **`std::atomic_ref`** | Non‑owning atomic wrapper for existing variables. | | **`std::string_view` enhancements** | `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `contains`, `transform`. | | **`std::variant`, `std::optional`, `std::any`** | Full constexpr support, move semantics, small‑object optimization. | | **`[[likely]]`, `[[unlikely]]` attributes** | Hints for branch prediction. | | **`std::array` changes** | `data()` now returns `T*` (not `const T*`), `constexpr` constructor. | | **Structured bindings** | `auto [a,b] = pair;` supports `enum` as tuple. | | **`noexcept` and `final` improvements** | `noexcept` deduction, `final` on constructors, destructor. | > **Bottom line:** C++20 introduced the bulk of the modern C++ toolbox – modules, concepts, coroutines, ranges, and a host of `constexpr`‑friendly library facilities that enable zero‑cost abstractions. ### Library (what’s new compared to C++17) | Section | New APIs (short) | |---------|-----------------| | `` | `bit_cast`, `popcount`, `countl_zero`, `countl_one`, `countr_zero`, `countr_one`. | | `` | `sys_days`, `utc_clock`, `time_zone`, `zoned_time`, `date` library. | | `` | `three_way` comparison operators (`<=>`). | | `` | Standard library concepts (`integral`, `floating_point`, etc.). | | `` | `std::format`, `std::vformat`, format specifiers. | | `` | `path`, `directory_iterator`, `file_status`, `last_write_time`. | | `` | **No** – added in C++23. | | `` | `std::reduce`, `std::inner_product` overloads. | | ``, ``, `` | Constexpr constructors, `value_or`, `transform`. | | `` | `span`, `subspan`. | | `` | `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `contains`. | | `` | `std::error_code` with `std::generic_category`. | | `` | `std::jthread` – thread with automatic join in destructor. | | `` | `is_swappable`, `is_nothrow_swappable`, etc. | | `` | `std::exchange`, `std::forward_like`, `std::move_if_noexcept`. | | `` | `views::all`, `views::transform`, `views::filter`, `actions`, `ranges::for_each`, `ranges::sort`. | | `` | `std::latch`, `std::barrier`, `std::atomic_ref`. | > **Note:** The module system was the *only* large language addition; the rest were library‑level. --- ## 2. C++23 – 2023 (finalized) C++23 largely refines and expands the C++20 foundation. The language itself remains almost unchanged – there are only a handful of small tweaks and new attributes. The bulk of the progress comes from **standard‑library** additions and polish. ### Language (tiny changes) | Feature | What it adds | |---------|--------------| | **`[[maybe_unused]]` on `constexpr` variables** | Avoids diagnostics when a constexpr variable is not used. | | **`concept` improvements** | `requires` clauses may now use `template<...>` for constraints, easier composition. | | **`consteval` overloads for `operator<=>`** | Enable `three_way` comparisons to be constexpr‑evalued in constant expressions. | | **`char8_t` const‑correctness** | `char8_t*` now points to mutable memory; `const char8_t*` for read‑only data. | | **`constexpr` `new`/`delete`** | Allowed in constant expressions; useful for `constexpr` containers. | | **`std::bit_cast` overloads** | Added `std::bit_cast` for any trivially copyable type (was already in C++20). | | **`std::span` constructors** | `std::span(T*)` now requires `T*` to be contiguous; added `size_type` overloads. | > **Bottom line:** C++23 does not break backward compatibility. The language rules are mostly unchanged; the value is in the library. ### Library – the real new stuff | Category | New/Finalized APIs | |----------|--------------------| | **``** | *Multi‑dimensional span* – a view of arbitrary‑rank, non‑owning, multidimensional arrays (used in BLAS, OpenCL, etc.). | | **``** |
  • `std::ranges::to` – convert a range into a container (`vector`, `list`, `array`, etc.).
  • `std::ranges::views::all_t` – a view that materializes a container into itself when passed to `ranges::to`.
  • `std::ranges::views::zip` (new) – zip two ranges together.
| | **``** | *Finalised* – all proposals for `std::format` are now officially part of the standard. Includes:
  • Locale‑aware format specifiers (`L`).
  • Custom formatters for user types (`std::formatter`).
  • New standard format specifiers for dates and times.
| | **``** | `std::string::starts_with`, `ends_with`, `contains`, `transform` – inherited from `std::string_view` but added to `std::string`. | | **``** | Added `std::erase_copy`, `std::erase_copy_if` (if not already present). | | **``** | `std::span::subspan` now has overloads for both `size_type` and `size_type` with a `count` – improves ergonomic slicing. | | **``** | `std::vector::shrink_to_fit` now `constexpr` in some cases (experimental). | | **``** | New concepts: `common_with`, `derived_from`, `movable`, `destructible`. | | **``** | `std::execution::par_unseq` was added to C++20; C++23 extends the library to allow `std::transform_reduce` overloads with execution policies. | | **``** | Added `std::make_error_code` overloads for `std::errc` in more contexts. | | **``** | `std::format_to` now supports output iterators that satisfy `std::output_iterator`. | | **``** | `std::jthread` now accepts `std::latch` and `std::barrier` in its `stop_token` API. | | **``** | Additional calendar features: `year_month_day_last`, `weekday_index` and new parsing/formatting functions. | | **``** | `std::gcd`, `std::lcm` (already C++17, but now constexpr). | | **``** | `std::array::fill` now `constexpr`. | | **``** | `std::formatter` is now constexpr‑friendly. | > **In short:** C++23’s library is the first to bring a *complete, fully specified* multi‑dimensional array view (`mdspan`), unify and finalise formatting, and polish the ranges library with a real conversion function (`ranges::to`). It also extends a handful of existing algorithms and containers to be more constexpr‑friendly. --- ## Quick Comparison Table | Feature | C++20 | C++23 | |---------|-------|-------| | Modules | Introduced | No change | | Concepts | Introduced | Improved syntax & `requires` clauses | | Coroutines | Introduced | No change | | Ranges | Introduced (`views`, `actions`) | Added `ranges::to`, `zip` view | | `constexpr` | Expanded (constexpr containers, consteval, constinit) | More `constexpr` in algorithms & containers | | `span` | Introduced | `subspan` overloads | | `format` | Introduced (provisional) | Finalised | | `mdspan` | Not in the standard | Added (multi‑dimensional view) | | `std::string` helpers (`starts_with`, etc.) | In `string_view` only | Added to `string` | | `erase` algorithms | Added (`erase`, `erase_if`, `erase_copy`, `erase_copy_if`) | No new ones | | `std::execution` policies | Introduced | Expanded with new overloads | | `jthread` | Introduced | Better stop‑token integration | --- ### Bottom line for practitioners | Category | C++20 | C++23 | |----------|-------|-------| | **Use if you need** | Compile‑time constraints, coroutines, ranges, modules, `constexpr` heavy code, `std::format` (initial version). | Want a fully standard formatting library, multi‑dimensional views, a cleaner ranges API (`to`, `zip`), or you’re using `string_view` helpers on `std::string`. | | **Compiler support** | GCC 10+, Clang 10+, MSVC 19.28+ have good support (full modules in MSVC 19.34). | GCC 13+, Clang 16+, MSVC 19.34+ include the library changes; the language changes are minor. | | **Migration** | If you’re already using C++20 features, upgrading to C++23 is largely a library‑level change – just add `-std=c++23` and fix any deprecation warnings. | New APIs (mdspan, ranges::to) need some code changes; otherwise, the transition is almost transparent. | --- ## Take‑away * **C++20**: A huge leap – new language constructs (modules, concepts, coroutines) and a modern, constexpr‑friendly library (ranges, `format`, `chrono`, `filesystem`, `span`). * **C++23**: The *refinement* stage – the library is tightened up, more expressive, and a few big new pieces (`mdspan`, `ranges::to`, final `format`) appear. The language stays almost the same. Feel free to ask for a deeper dive on any specific feature, or a migration checklist for moving an existing C++20 codebase to C++23!
